header.userPrompt:
Add two non-blocking confirm-time warnings when a user confirms a bank-statement draft, so suspicious statements are flagged but still importable.

Background: a recent change (search git log / PRs for "cardMismatchWarnings") added non-blocking confirm warnings in the draft-confirm flow. The object `BankStatementConfirmChecks` holds the check helpers and `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction` wires them in, producing `ConfirmWarning` values that flow through the existing `acceptWarnings` gate: when warnings are present and the client did not pass acceptWarnings=true, the confirm is blocked with the warnings returned; when acceptWarnings=true it proceeds. Follow that exact pattern (same object, same action, same gate, same ConfirmWarning type). Study that prior implementation first and mirror its structure, style, and tests.

Add these two warnings, both derived from the draft's statement rows (each row has a transaction date) and the draft's declared period [periodStart, periodEnd]:

WARNING 1 — rows outside the declared period:
Fire when one or more draft rows have a date before periodStart or after periodEnd. Cause can be benign (a prepaid/virtual card whose cycle legitimately spans two calendar months) or a parser error, so it is a warning, not an error: the user inspects the statement and confirms. Message must state how many rows fall outside the stated period, the stated period, and the earliest and latest out-of-range dates. If every row is out of range, still fire (that is exactly the total-misparse case worth flagging).

WARNING 2 — rows dated inside another same-card statement's period:
Fire when one or more draft rows have a date that falls within the [periodStart, periodEnd] of an EXISTING confirmed statement of the SAME card (same bank name + product type + last 4 + currency key already used by the prior mismatch check). This is the dangerous duplicate-import case that the existing period-range overlap check (findOverlapping) misses, because the declared periods themselves do not overlap yet an individual row lands inside the other statement's period. Message must name the offending row date(s) and identify which existing statement's period they fall into. Reuse the same-card statement fetch the prior mismatch check already performs rather than adding a new query; extend it if it does not already expose the existing statements' periods.

Both warnings may fire together on the same statement (a 2025-11-27 row in a 2025-12-01..2025-12-31 draft is both outside the December period and inside November's period); that is fine, emit both.

Limits: when listing offending dates/rows in a message, show at most the first 5 and then "+N more" so a fully-misparsed statement cannot produce an unbounded message.

Constraints (this repo):
- Prefer pure, side-effect-free check functions that take the rows + period (+ existing same-card statements) and return the warnings, unit-tested directly without a DB, exactly as the prior mismatch check is tested. Wire those into the action.
- All DB queries (reads and writes) must be user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?) and list queries must have ORDER BY. Do not add DB CHECK constraints or column defaults; validation stays at app level.
- Use Chimney transformInto for any case-class shape mapping rather than manual field copying.
- Tests must not hit any external API: use the existing testcontainers Postgres and fakes.
- Custom wart NamedArguments: when a call passes 2+ arguments of the same type they MUST be passed by name or compilation fails.
- Do not auto-correct or mutate the statement period or row dates; only warn.

Acceptance criteria:
- `CI=true sbt Test/compile` compiles; scalafmt is clean.
- New unit tests cover: warning 1 fires for rows before periodStart, for rows after periodEnd, and for all-rows-out-of-range; does not fire when all rows are within period. Warning 2 fires when a row date lands inside an existing same-card statement's period and does not fire for a different card or when no existing statement covers the date. Message capping to 5 + "+N more" is covered.
- The confirm action blocks with these warnings when acceptWarnings is not set and proceeds when it is, consistent with the prior mismatch warning.

resultJson.description:
Add two non-blocking confirm-time warnings to the bank-statement draft-confirm flow so suspicious statements are flagged but can still be imported: (1) RowsOutsidePeriod — one or more draft rows are dated before periodStart or after periodEnd (a benign cross-month prepaid cycle, or a parser misread; still fires when every row is out of range); (2) RowsInOtherStatement — one or more draft rows are dated inside the [periodStart, periodEnd] of an existing confirmed statement of the same account (same bank name + product type + last4 + currency). The second check catches the dangerous duplicate-import case that the existing period-overlap check (`findOverlapping`) misses, where the declared periods don't overlap but individual rows do.

Both follow the pattern of the earlier card-mismatch warnings exactly. Pure check functions in `BankStatementConfirmChecks` return `ConfirmWarning`s with new `ConfirmWarningKind` cases. `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction` appends them to its `warnings` list, so the existing `acceptWarnings` gate applies unchanged: the confirm is blocked and returns the warnings unless `acceptWarnings = true`, in which case the statement is created. Nothing is corrected: the period and row dates are stored exactly as in the draft. Any message that lists dates shows at most 5 entries, followed by "+N more".

For warning 2 we add no new query. The existing same-card fetch (`findSameCardMismatches`, bank + last4) currently filters out statements with the same type and currency, so it can't see the exact-account statements warning 2 needs. It is broadened to return every statement of that card. `cardMismatchWarnings` already ignores values equal to the draft's, so its behaviour doesn't change. Warning 2 then keeps only the statements whose type and currency also match, in memory.

tasks.title: Add RowsOutsidePeriod / RowsInOtherStatement warning kinds and pure checks
tasks.description:
In lib/api/shared .../bankstatements/ConfirmWarning.scala, add `case object RowsOutsidePeriod extends ConfirmWarningKind("RowsOutsidePeriod")` and `case object RowsInOtherStatement extends ConfirmWarningKind("RowsInOtherStatement")`, and append both to `values`. ConfirmWarningSpec loops over `values`, so it covers the JSON round trip without changes.

In server .../validations/BankStatementConfirmChecks.scala, add two pure functions that the action does not call yet:

(a) `rowsOutsidePeriodWarning(rowDates: List[LocalDate], periodStart: LocalDate, periodEnd: LocalDate): Option[ConfirmWarning]`. A row is out of range when its date is before periodStart or after periodEnd (inclusive bounds). Return None when no row is out of range. The message must state the number of out-of-range rows (e.g. "N of M rows"), the stated period as "$start → $end", and the earliest and latest out-of-range dates. It must still fire when every row is out of range, including a reversed period (start after end). Do not alter any dates.

(b) `rowsInOtherStatementWarning(metadata: BankStatement.Metadata, rowDates: List[LocalDate], sameCard: List[BankStatement]): Option[ConfirmWarning]`. First keep only the `sameCard` statements whose bankName, productType, accountLast4 and currency all equal the metadata (exact equality, matching the DAO's `findOverlapping`). For each remaining statement, in input order, collect the distinct, sorted row dates inside [s.periodStart, s.periodEnd] (inclusive). Return one warning that names the offending dates and the existing period ("s.periodStart → s.periodEnd") they fall into, or None if no date matches. Fire whether or not the declared periods also overlap; don't deduplicate against the Overlap warning.

Add a private helper, e.g. `capped(items: List[String]): String`, that shows the first 5 items and then "+N more". Apply it to the dates listed per statement and to the list of statement groups.

Update the object's docs to match. Calls that pass 2+ arguments of the same type (the LocalDates, and the two Lists in b) must use named arguments, or the NamedArguments wart fails the build.

In BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec (server/src/test/.../actions/bankstatements/), add `"rowsOutsidePeriodWarning" should` and `"rowsInOtherStatementWarning" should` blocks in the existing style. Use the `statement(start, end)` helper and `.copy(...)` for card fields, plus a `BankStatement.Metadata` fixture. Cover:
- W1 fires for a row before periodStart, for a row after periodEnd, and when every row is out of range; it does not fire when all rows are inside, including rows exactly on the boundary days.
- The W1 message includes the count, the period, and the earliest and latest dates.
- W2 fires when a row date lands inside an existing same-account statement's period (e.g. a 2025-11-27 row in a 2025-12-01..2025-12-31 draft against a 2025-11-01..2025-11-30 statement; the message includes 2025-11-27 and "2025-11-01 → 2025-11-30").
- W2 does not fire for a different card (other last4 / bank / productType / currency), when no existing statement covers the date, or for an empty list.
- Capping: 7 offending dates produce a message with the first 5 and "+2 more" but not the 6th or 7th date.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec *ConfirmWarningSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Broaden the same-card fetch to return all statements of the card
tasks.description:
Rename `BankStatementDAO.findSameCardMismatches` and `BankStatementRepository.findSameCardMismatches` to `findSameCard(userId, metadata)`. Drop the `AND (product_type <> ... OR currency <> ...)` clause and keep `WHERE user_id = ?`, `bank_name`, `account_last4` and `ORDER BY period_start, id`. Update both docstrings: it returns every statement of the same card (bank + last4) regardless of type, currency or period, and is used for the type/currency mismatch check and the rows-in-other-statement check.

In ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction, call `findSameCard` and pass the result to `cardMismatchWarnings`. It already filters out values equal to the draft's, so its behaviour doesn't change; update its scaladoc reference from `findSameCardMismatches` to `findSameCard`.

In BankStatementRepositorySpec, rename the `"findSameCardMismatches" should` block. Change "not match the exact same card, type and currency" so it now expects the statement to be returned. Keep the other-last4/other-bank and other-user exclusion tests, and keep a test that different type/currency statements are returned in period_start order.

Add no new query and no DB constraint. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"`: the existing mismatch controller tests must still pass unchanged.

tasks.title: Wire the date warnings into ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction and cover the gate end-to-end
tasks.description:
In ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.apply, compute `rowDates = payload.transactions.map(_.date)` and append to `warnings`, after the existing period/overlap/card-mismatch warnings:
- `BankStatementConfirmChecks.rowsOutsidePeriodWarning(rowDates = ..., periodStart = metadata.periodStart, periodEnd = metadata.periodEnd).toList`
- `BankStatementConfirmChecks.rowsInOtherStatementWarning(metadata = metadata, rowDates = rowDates, sameCard = sameCard).toList`, reusing the `findSameCard` result already fetched for the mismatch check (no new query).

Update the class scaladoc's list of warnings. Leave the acceptWarnings gate and `create` untouched: row dates and the period are stored as-is.

Update the existing BankStatementDraftControllerSpec assertions that now see extra kinds:
- The Overlap tests that confirm the same Jan payload twice (around lines 420-446 and 647-663) also get RowsInOtherStatement. Expect `List(Overlap, RowsInOtherStatement)`.
- The PeriodOrder test (reversed Jan period, Jan 15 row) also gets RowsOutsidePeriod. Expect both kinds.
- In the FuturePeriod test, move the transaction date inside the generated period (e.g. `end.minusDays(10)`) so the test stays focused on FuturePeriod.

After running the spec, fix any other assertion that now sees the new kinds in the same way.

Add controller tests built with `seedReadyDraft` and `cardPayload`/`reconcilingPayload`, changing only transaction dates so the drafts still reconcile:
1. A draft with a row dated after periodEnd returns `bankStatementId = None` with `List(RowsOutsidePeriod)`, and the draft remains. Confirming with acceptWarnings=true creates the statement, keeps the original row date and period, and deletes the draft.
2. Confirm a Jan cardPayload, then a Feb cardPayload whose row is dated 2026-01-28. It is blocked with `List(RowsOutsidePeriod, RowsInOtherStatement)`, the message includes "2026-01-28" and "2026-01-01 → 2026-01-31", and only 1 statement exists. With acceptWarnings=true it is created.
3. The same as 2 but with a different accountLast4 or currency on the second card gets no RowsInOtherStatement; currency/type differences may still raise the existing mismatch kinds, so assert on the absence of RowsInOtherStatement.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec"`, then `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/: Tapir endpoints and models shared by server and web. The warning type lives at lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/ConfirmWarning.scala:
  - `sealed abstract class ConfirmWarningKind(val entryName: String)`, with case objects Overlap, PeriodLength, PeriodOrder, FuturePeriod, ProductTypeMismatch, CurrencyMismatch.
  - `val values: Seq[ConfirmWarningKind]` must list every case; the JSON Format looks kinds up by entryName.
  - `case class ConfirmWarning(kind: ConfirmWarningKind, message: String)`.
  - lib/api/shared/src/test/.../ConfirmWarningSpec.scala round-trips every `values` entry.
  - web/ doesn't match on kinds; it just shows messages, so no frontend change is needed.
- server/: Play backend, layered controllers → actions → repositories (Anorm DAOs).

KEY FILES
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/validations/BankStatementConfirmChecks.scala: pure, non-blocking checks. Existing functions:
  - `periodWarnings(start, end, today): List[ConfirmWarning]`
  - `overlapWarning(overlapping: List[BankStatement]): Option[ConfirmWarning]`
  - `cardMismatchWarnings(metadata: BankStatement.Metadata, existing: List[BankStatement]): List[ConfirmWarning]`, which does `existing.map(_.productType).distinct.filterNot(_ == metadata.productType)` (same for currency), so passing it statements with matching values is harmless.
  - Style: `Option.when(cond)(ConfirmWarning(Kind, s"..."))`, periods rendered as s"$start → $end" (U+2192 arrow), card as s"••••${last4}".
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.scala: `apply(draftId, userId, acceptWarnings, acceptUnverified)`. It:
  - loads the draft and parses `payload: BankStatementDraft.Payload` (api model);
  - runs `requireReconciled`, then `metadata = requireMetadata(payload.metadata)`, giving `BankStatement.Metadata(bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart: LocalDate, periodEnd: LocalDate)`;
  - fetches `overlapping <- bankStatementRepository.findOverlapping(userId, metadata)` and `mismatches <- bankStatementRepository.findSameCardMismatches(userId, metadata)`;
  - builds `warnings = periodWarnings(...) ++ overlapWarning(...).toList ++ cardMismatchWarnings(metadata, mismatches)`;
  - gate: `if (warnings.nonEmpty && !acceptWarnings) Future.successful(Confirm.Response(None, warnings)) else create(...)`, and create also returns the warnings.
  - Rows come from `payload.transactions: List[BankStatementDraft.Transaction(date: LocalDate, amount, description, txnType, runningBalance)]`.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala:
  - `findOverlapping` (~line 183): exact bank + product + last4 + currency, inclusive period overlap, ORDER BY period_start, id.
  - `findSameCardMismatches` (~line 202): bank + last4 AND (type <> OR currency <>), ORDER BY period_start, id.
  - Both select `id, document_id, user_id, #$metadataColumns, created_at, updated_at` with `parser.*`.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala: wraps the DAO calls in `Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => ... } }` (~lines 118-128).
- `repositories.models.BankStatement` (case class) has id, documentId, userId, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, createdAt, updatedAt (+ acceptedUnverified etc.; see the test helper below for the constructor used in unit tests).

TESTS
- Unit: server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec.scala (package net.wiringbits.actions.bankstatements). It uses AnyWordSpec + must.Matchers and a `statement(start: String, end: String): BankStatement` helper (BBVA/debit/EUR/1234), customised with `.copy(...)`. The cardMismatchWarnings block builds a `BankStatement.Metadata` fixture. There's no DB; mirror this style for the new checks.
- Repository (testcontainers Postgres): server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala.
  - `"findSameCardMismatches" should` block is at ~line 1067.
  - Uses `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, `createUser().futureValue` and `seed(userId, metadata): UUID`.
- Controller/integration: server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala.
  - Fixtures: `reconcilingPayload` (BBVA/debit/EUR/1234, Jan 2026 period, one row on 2026-01-15, reconciles 100 → 60) and `cardPayload(productType="debit", currency="EUR", bankName="Test Bank", accountLast4="0000", february=false)` (Feb = 2026-02-01..28 with a row on 2026-02-15). `unverifiablePayload` is Test Bank/0000, Jan, row on Jan 15, no balances.
  - `seedReadyDraft(userId, payload): UUID`; `client.confirmBankStatementDraft(id, acceptWarnings = ..., acceptUnverified = ...)` returns `Response(bankStatementId: Option[UUID], warnings)`.
  - Also used: `client.getBankStatements.futureValue.data`, `client.listBankStatementDrafts.futureValue.drafts`, `client.getBankStatement(id)`, `withApiClient { implicit client => ... }`, `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)`.
  - Changing only transaction dates keeps a payload reconciling.
  - IMPORTANT: several existing assertions expect exact kind lists (`must be(List(ConfirmWarningKind.Overlap))`, etc.). Once wired, the Overlap tests that confirm identical Jan payloads twice also get RowsInOtherStatement, the reversed-period PeriodOrder test also gets RowsOutsidePeriod, and the FuturePeriod test (period near today, row 2026-01-15) also gets RowsOutsidePeriod.

CONVENTIONS / GOTCHAS
- Custom wart NamedArguments: any call passing 2+ arguments of the same type must name them (e.g. periodStart/periodEnd LocalDates, two Lists), or compilation fails.
- DB: every query must have `WHERE user_id = ?`, and list queries need ORDER BY. No DB CHECK constraints or defaults.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` / `into` for case-class shape mapping (the action already imports `io.scalaland.chimney.dsl.*`).
- Never mutate or auto-correct periods or row dates; only warn. Throw RuntimeException for hard failures (existing style); warnings are non-blocking.
- Message lists are capped: first 5 items, then "+N more".
- Verify with targeted runs only: `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec"`, `*BankStatementRepositorySpec`, `*BankStatementDraftControllerSpec`, `*ConfirmWarningSpec`, plus `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`. Don't run the full `sbt test`.
- Docs: docs/guide/{backend,testing,antipatterns,data-infra}.md.
